question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{2x}.$ Its derivative is given by 

$$
{y}^{′}=2(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{2x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{2x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{2x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =2x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(2x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x))+(2x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =2\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+2x\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}\cdot {sec}^{2}⁡x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+2x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =2(\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x\,)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we substitute $y=(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{2x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)^{2x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{tan}⁡x)+x\operatorname{csc}⁡x\,\operatorname{sec}⁡x.$
